data.title: Mass Account Lockout or Removal Achievable
data.summary:
A compromised administrative account could disable, lock out or remove user accounts in
bulk, including the accounts required to respond to the incident.
data.description:
Removing access is the move that converts an intrusion into a crisis, because it takes away
the organisation's ability to respond. Where the responders' own accounts live in the same
directory as everything else, the first action of a sophisticated intrusion is to remove
them.

Recovery then depends on break-glass credentials that are outside the compromised
directory, stored where they remain retrievable when normal access is gone, and tested.
All three conditions are frequently unmet — most often the third.

This is a planning finding as much as a technical one, and it belongs in front of the
people who own incident response rather than only the directory team.
data.recommendation:
* Maintain break-glass accounts outside the production directory, with credentials stored
  so they remain retrievable during an outage.
* Test break-glass access on a schedule; untested credentials routinely fail when needed.
* Alert on bulk account modification and on changes to accounts belonging to the response
  team.
* Ensure the incident response plan does not depend on systems that authenticate against
  the compromised directory.
data.short_recommendation: Maintain and test break-glass accounts outside the production directory.
